cells.tense: Something is arriving at the source, and the reach toward it is already sound.
cells.act: draw the shape of it without the details
cells.ask: Put the shape of what's arriving on a single page — no story, no specifics, just the curve. Once is enough.
cells.core:
Something's arriving at your door and the leaning toward it feels less like a surprise and more like recognition. The pull had a direction before this thing showed up, and the direction was tended long enough that it now runs without prompting. That's why the timing is usable and why you don't have to talk yourself into wanting it.

Here's the next step: get the shape of what's arriving down in one place, stripped of the story. Not the specifics, not who said what — the curve underneath. Once you can see the shape, you'll know where it fits and where it doesn't, and the bracing for it to be something else will let up. The pattern is yours to keep. The details can wait.
cells.sheetLine: What's arriving matches a direction you already carried.
cells.place: Where what was outside turns to enter

cells.tense: You are already living past this arrival, lit for a version that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Hold off on what's arriving until one part of it plainly matters. Then give that part your attention, and nothing else gets touched today.
cells.core:
Something's coming, and you're already three steps beyond it, glowing about where it will end up. The brightness is real. It's also outrunning the thing itself — you're lit about a version that hasn't landed, while what's actually at your door waits there while you describe what it'll become.

Start smaller than the glow wants. Hold off on what's arriving until one part of it shows itself as the part that matters — not the part that could matter someday, the one that does. Then give that part your attention. Nothing spoils from waiting an hour or a day, and what lands after the pause tends to hold better than what got lit up before it.
cells.sheetLine: The lift is outrunning the thing that's arriving.

cells.tense: You stood at that door a long while, and what was supposed to come through didn't.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Tend something young and unimpressive — a plant, a page, a short sit. No goal, nothing recorded, no result asked of it at all.
cells.core:
You stopped expecting much from the door. Things kept not landing, and hope that keeps not landing wears through. So here you are at the source with the reach gone quiet — not from giving up exactly, but because showing up started costing more than it returned. The cultivation ran long and nothing flowered.

Try tending something young anyway, and ask nothing back from it. Not the big wish. Something minor — a plant, a page, a short practice — with no goal attached and nothing counted. Let it stay unimpressive beside the old hope. You're not reviving the big one. You're keeping the ground under it alive, so something can root here in its own time rather than yours.
cells.sheetLine: You tend things well. Nothing has tended you back.

cells.tense: You are already radiating toward what's arriving, and you don't count that as what this is.
cells.act: bear the next hour of it without deciding anything
cells.ask: Take the next stretch with what's arriving without deciding anything about it. Move neither toward it nor away. Hold your ground a while with it undecided.
cells.core:
You've started turning toward whatever is arriving, and the lean shows to the people near you — the light, the tilt. Asked, you'd probably say you're keeping your options open, nothing settled. The turning is being done by you. From the inside it reads as ordinary.

Stay standing where you already are for another stretch before anything moves. Not toward, not away — just here, with the thing, and no decision attached to it. If the question comes up, you can say you're holding. The pull doesn't need you to name it. It needs you to stop filing it under nothing. What's arriving will meet you where you stand either way.
